title: Named, swappable scene palettes: colours reached by their role in one central Palettes, starting from the trade scene
description:
Scenes pick raw `Color` constants or index a `Palette` by number, so the same job gets a different colour in every scene and trying a new look means rewriting the scene. Make colour a function of its role, held in swappable named palettes defined in one place.

What the inventory of the menu, knot editor, trade scene, GLSL code pane, model scene and its menu, and DSL graph viewer found:
- UI roles disagree across scenes: muted text is GREY_DARK (menu), BLUE_GREY (code pane) and BROWN_GREY (trade); clickable text has four colours; headings are YELLOW_ORANGE in one menu section and IXDAR in the next; error is RED, RED_LIGHT, BLACK, or the float colour for "?Missing?"; BLUE_GREY means muted text, link text, edge lines, scroll thumb and a mesh tint.
- Domain colours are copied between files (cut/match colours in `Drawing` and `NegativeCutMatchViewTool`) or hidden behind indices: `Palettes.GLSL_VECTOR_COMPONENT.color(i)` in `GLSLParseText`, `roleColors[textRole]` in `DslGraphView`, and TRADE-23's `Palettes.TRADE`/`TRADE_COMPANY` read through int role constants.
- Id cycles and ramps (RING, REGION, PATCH, BRIGHT_PATCH, OVERLAY_GROUP, EDGE_MARK, SCALAR_RAMP, DSL_TIME_SHARE) are what `Palette` is for; indexing is right there.

Design:
- `Theme`: the UI roles every scene shares, as named fields: text, mutedText, headingText, linkText, selectedText, hoverFlash, accent, success, warning, error, background, panel, panelBorder, line, gridLine, scrollTrack, scrollThumb. The shared widgets read the drawing scene's theme instead of hardcoding: HyperString's default text, InfoPane, Terminal and its commands, tooltips, MenuBox/MenuItem/MenuScrollBar, ErrorToasts, SceneModelMenu/SceneCollectionMenu. The hover flash becomes one theme rule instead of three ColorLerp variants.
- One palette class per scene with named domain roles and a `ui` theme: `TradePalette` (player, rival, road, river, bridge, grid, cargo, gold, goldLight, dry), `CodePalette` (keyword, type, function, number, operator, punctuation, vectorX/Y/Z/W, booleanResult, skipped), `KnotPalette` (tourPath, cut, cutHighlight, match, matchHighlight, knotPoint, externalSegment), `GraphPalette` (nodeBorder, criticalPath, edge, port, groupFrame, titleText, typeText, timingText, literalText, timeShare ramp), `ModelPalette` (meshFill, meshEdge, markedRing, geodesicDraft, creaseDraft, anchor roles, dimmedRegion, unlabelledRegion, and its id cycles). Code reads a palette by name then role: `palette.road`, `palette.ui.mutedText`; no indices.
- Every value lives in `Palettes.java` as named instances pointing at `Color` constants (`DARK_THEME`, `PAPER_THEME`, `TRADE_PAPER`, `TRADE_NIGHT`, `CODE_PASTEL`, ...), with an options list per kind. The palette classes only declare the roles.
- Each scene holds a `palette` field; assigning another instance re-colours the scene. A control (key or terminal `palette next`) and an automation route cycle a scene through its options so a script can screenshot every candidate.
- `Palette` keeps only id cycles and ramps; scene palettes reference the cycles they use.
- Enforcement: an autofix checkstyle rule that names a `Color` constant only in `Color.java` and `Palettes.java`, so scene, tool and widget code must go through a palette; a test that every palette instance sets every role and keeps text readable on its background.

The trade scene is the first draft: TRADE-23's scene already draws every colour from one lookup per role (`role(...)`, `company(...)`), so converting it to `TradePalette` with `TRADE_PAPER` and a second option proves the shape before the shared widgets and the other scenes move.

Proposed dark-theme resolutions of today's conflicts (to confirm): body text WHITE, heading YELLOW_ORANGE, muted GREY_DARK, link TEAL_BLUE_LIGHT, selected GREEN_TEAL_LIGHT, error RED; IXDAR becomes the accent/logo colour rather than default text.

User 2026-10-27, review of the first attempt: 'there should be ONE pallete class, and no themes or any knotpallete or codepallete, ONE'. The first attempt's Theme plus per-scene palette classes are rejected; the definition of done is rewritten around one Palette class.

definition-of-done:
1. There is ONE palette class, `Palette`: named fields for colour functions (text, mutedText, heading, link, selected, highlight, hover, accent, success, warning, error, background, panel, border, line, grid, ...) plus its id cycles and ramps as named fields. No Theme, ScenePalette, KnotPalette, CodePalette, GraphPalette, ModelPalette, QuadLayoutPalette or TradePalette classes exist.
2. Every value lives in `Palettes.java` as named `Palette` instances (at least two: a dark one and a paper/light one) and an options list; nowhere else.
3. Each scene holds one `palette` field and draws everything through it by function (`palette.line`, `palette.mutedText`); scene concepts (road, cut, keyword, player) map onto the shared functions rather than getting their own role. No class-token or fallback lookup.
4. The trade scene is converted first and draws only through the palette; then the shared widgets, GLSL code pane, DSL graph viewer, knot editor and model scenes.
5. A key/terminal command and an automation route swap a scene's palette; screenshots of every scene in every option, plus before/after, are under tmp/.
6. The autofix rule refuses a `Color` constant named anywhere except `Color.java` and `Palettes.java`, on by default, with no exemptions, and the build is green.
7. A unit test checks every palette instance sets every field and text contrasts with background and panel.

8. Palettes are interchangeable: any palette instance can be assigned to any scene (e.g. the knot editor wearing the trade scene's palette and vice versa) and renders readably; cycling in any scene steps through every palette in Palettes. Screenshots show the knot editor in the paper palette and the trade scene in the dark palette.
testing-plan:
1. Unit test over every palette instance: no role null; text/background contrast above a threshold in each theme.
2. Cycle the trade scene through its palette options with the automation route and screenshot each; do the same for the code pane, DSL graph, knot editor and model scene.
3. Before/after screenshots of each scene under the default dark theme to confirm only the intended conflicts changed.
4. mvn -q compile with the new checkstyle rule on is clean; ColorOrderTest still passes.
unknowns: Which colour wins each conflicting role in the default dark theme (proposed: body WHITE, heading YELLOW_ORANGE, muted GREY_DARK, link TEAL_BLUE_LIGHT, selected GREEN_TEAL_LIGHT, error RED)
How the shared widgets find the theme: the scene they draw in, or a theme passed down
Whether the checkstyle rule lands in autofix in this ticket or a follow-up once every scene is migrated
changes-made: Theme (shared UI roles plus the code pane's CodePalette and a single hover rule, Theme.hover) and per-scene palettes ScenePalette, KnotPalette, ModelPalette (with GraphPalette and QuadLayoutPalette), TradePalette; every value is in Palettes (DARK/SLATE/PAPER themes, KNOT_DARK/SLATE, MODEL_DARK/SLATE, TRADE_PAPER/NIGHT, CODE_PASTEL/VIVID). Scenes hold a palette field; paletteOptions() and cyclePalette() swap it, through the terminal 'palette [next|list|name]' and POST /ui/palette. Shared widgets, terminal commands, code pane, DSL graph (named roles instead of roleColors[]), knot editor and tools, model/ring/mesh scenes and tools, anatomy demos converted; GLSL_VECTOR_COMPONENT replaced by vectorX..W. autofix ColorConstantOutsidePaletteCheck refuses Color constants outside the color package, off by default and on in Ixdar's pom (colorPaletteSeverity=error); the old trade game is exempt until TRADE-24 merges and moves onto TradePalette. PaletteRolesTest checks every role is set and text contrast. Screenshots tmp/ui17-*.png.

Rework after review: ONE Palette class (26 fields: text, mutedText, headingText, linkText, selected, disabled, highlight, hover, accent, success, warning, error, background, panel, panelBorder, surface, line, gridLine; cycles categories, ring, region, patch, overlayGroup, edgeMark; ramps scalar, timeShare; hovered(c) is the one hover rule). Theme, ScenePalette and the per-scene palette classes are deleted. Palettes holds DARK, SLATE, PAPER and OPTIONS; every scene steps through all of OPTIONS (palette command, POST /ui/palette); the trade scene wears PAPER by default and was converted. Scene.activePalette() replaces currentTheme/currentPalette. autofix ColorConstantOutsidePaletteCheck is on by default (error) and allows only Color.java and Palettes.java; Ixdar's pom override and trade exemption are gone. PaletteRolesTest checks every field is set, OPTIONS is every palette, and text contrast. Screenshots: tmp/ui17-<scene>-<palette>.png from tmp/palette_shots.sh.
review-summary: Every scene now draws through a named palette (Theme plus TradePalette, KnotPalette, ModelPalette, CodePalette, GraphPalette) whose values live only in Palettes, and a checkstyle rule keeps Color constants out of scene code. Swapping a palette re-colours a scene, so a new look no longer means rewriting it.
